entities.name: Laud of Coutances
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Laud of Coutances was the fifth bishop of Coutances and a prominent figure in the Roman Catholic Church during the Classical era. Born into a noble family, he rose to prominence through his piety and administrative skills, eventually becoming bishop in 500 CE.

As bishop, Laud played a crucial role in the development of the Christian faith in Gaul (modern-day France) and was instrumental in the establishment of the Abbey of Sainte-Trinité de Cormoréns. His legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he was canonized as a saint by both the Roman Catholic and Eastern Orthodox Churches.

Laud's significance lies in his role as a unifying figure for the Christian community during a time of religious upheaval, and his contributions to the development of monasticism in Gaul. His story serves as a testament to the power of faith and leadership in shaping the course of human history.

The inscription on Laud's tomb at Sainte-Trinité de Cormoréns reads: 'In hoc sepulto Ludovicus de Cunucensis, episcopus quintus, qui Christi fide et virtute nobilitavit Gallaeciam.' ('Here lies Ludovicus of Coutances, fifth bishop, who nobleized Gaul through his faith and virtue in Christ.')
